questions.title: Who provides water and sewer, and what capacity is committed?
questions.evidence: The preserved county packet names Regional Utilities for water and sewer (PDF p. 3 / printed staff p. 2). The utility plan names South Walton Utility Company for water and Florida Community Services for sewer (PDF p. 34 / sheet 11 of 17). Both pages were visually reinspected for this preview against the preserved, fingerprinted packet. This verifies the document mismatch, not the actual provider or inadequate capacity.
questions.favorable: A table correction or different company names may reconcile the records. A mismatch does not demonstrate insufficient service. No current capacity failure, dangerous leak or contamination is established.
questions.missing: Signed parcel-specific water and sewer commitments; connection points and asset ownership; reserved and unbuilt demand; permitted/design, average, peak and wet-weather demand; local network studies and dated incident/pressure records.
questions.custodian: County Planning holds the project review file. South Walton Utility and Regional Utilities hold their service/commitment records; DEP drinking-water and wastewater programs hold their respective regulatory records. Utility public-records status is not presumed.
questions.decision: County reviewing/issuing authority for MAJ26-000007; each utility for its service commitment and regulators within their permit jurisdiction. The operative order must identify the remaining decision stage.
questions.next: Compare signed utility letters and accepted connection drawings to the plan and staff table; reconcile demand and reservations using existing records, with plant and local-network capacity assessed separately.
questions.criterion: Providers, connection/ownership boundaries, phase-specific commitments and capacity basis are documented consistently; any required capacity safeguards have a named owner, trigger and verification record.

questions.title: Which adopted stormwater requirements govern Raven?
questions.evidence: AO02 is witness testimony (printed p. 49 lines 6-17 / PDF p. 13; printed pp. 52-53 / PDF p. 14). AO04 p. 1 (February 5, 2020) interprets the 1984 action; AO08 p. 1 (May 11, 2010) seeks clarification. AO11 pp. 2-3 (May 30, 2014) states a historical agency position. These are distinct from adopted controlling text. Raven staff lists a 25-year event (packet p. 3).
questions.favorable: The record includes county-approved-plan interpretations and favorable findings under some county criteria. Historical disagreement does not establish today’s controlling standard or a Raven violation. AO07 notes, AO14 advocacy slides and AO15 proposed criteria are not adopted amendments.
questions.missing: Complete operative DRI order, incorporated standards/exhibits, adopted amendments and any rescissions; Raven permits, conditions and written review basis tying each requirement to this parcel and phase.
questions.custodian: County Planning for orders/amendments and review closure; DEP and NWFWMD for their permits and retained historical correspondence. Record custodians are asked for existing records, not a new legal analysis.
questions.decision: County approving authority and the applicable permitting agency within its own authority; current operative approvals must establish which decisions remain.
questions.next: Build a dated adoption chain and compare it with the Raven engineering criteria and permit coverage. Preserve rainfall, runoff and storm-duration distinctions.
questions.criterion: Each applicable standard has an adopted source, effective date, amendment history, phase/parcel scope and documented engineering compliance basis; unresolved conflicts are explicitly addressed by the responsible reviewer.

questions.title: What project-specific evidence demonstrates development will not worsen flooding or pollution?
questions.evidence: Staff reports proposed compensatory storage, a 25-year/24-hour design analysis and no outstanding floodplain issues (packet pp. 6-7 / staff pp. 5-6); environmental review reports no observed onsite contamination (packet p. 8 / staff p. 7). These scoped findings should be tested alongside current project drainage and operational records.
questions.favorable: AO01 p. 1 (March 31, 2025) reports compliance of inspected DEP ponds, not blanket Raven clearance. AO12 printed p. 31 / PDF p. 35 pairs historical DRI deficiencies with favorable interior-system and shared-outfall findings. No hydraulic link to Raven follows from proximity, and no current pollution causation is established.
questions.missing: Raven native model and inputs, boundary/tailwater assumptions, accepted as-builts, outfall/connection mapping, inspections and maintenance, incident and sampling records; permit coverage and review closure. AO12 appendices are absent.
questions.custodian: County Planning/engineering for project review; DEP and NWFWMD for jurisdiction-specific permits/inspections; utilities for utility assets and incidents. Developer/engineer supplies design support through the review file.
questions.decision: County technical reviewers and issuing authority; permitting agencies within their jurisdiction. Independent technical review is a community request unless an operative condition requires it.
questions.next: Review the project-specific model and accepted records, distinguish existing from proposed conditions, and match any incident to its asset, date and drainage basin before drawing a causal conclusion.
questions.criterion: A reproducible phase-specific analysis documents boundary conditions and effects; applicable safeguards specify measurable thresholds, monitoring/maintenance ownership, corrective triggers and how completion will be verified.

questions.title: Which enforceable recreation and open-space commitments must be preserved?
questions.evidence: The narrative and allocation letter require reconciliation of development/open-space scope (packet pp. 15-16 and 77-78). AO13 p. 2 is a historical Parcel 561 inquiry, not a ruling on Raven. AO09’s majority ends where the concurrence begins at PDF p. 18; reversal/remand does not invalidate all Raven approvals.
questions.favorable: AO09 records the absence of objection to the 2016 NOPC and rescission of the 2014 DONC in 2017. Open-space designation alone does not prove a public recreation right or unlawful loss. Later operative amendments and orders may change the analysis.
questions.missing: Controlling recreation/open-space conditions and amendments, current Exhibit E and parcel ledger, recorded easements/rights, conversion approvals and acreage reconciliation; operative later court orders.
questions.custodian: County Planning for approval/exhibit records; Clerk/official records for recorded instruments and court orders; owners/association for retained commitments. Court records and private recreation rights require separate review.
questions.decision: County authority responsible for the operative approval, and parties charged with enforceable recorded commitments; legal effect depends on the controlling instrument.
questions.next: Reconcile parcel and DRI-wide acreage against the operative exhibits and recorded rights; identify whether each commitment is public, private, amendable or already amended.
questions.criterion: Protected acreage and enforceable rights are mapped and reconciled with the adopted record; any authorized change and required replacement/mitigation are documented, with responsible parties and verification steps.
